title: Maintenance Tech (PRN)
description:
The Plant Operations / Maintenance Technician is responsible for the safe, reliable, and efficient operation, maintenance, and repair of the hospital’s physical plant, mechanical systems, and facility infrastructure. In a Critical Access Hospital setting, this role ensures uninterrupted operation of essential systems that support patient care, safety, and regulatory compliance. The technician performs preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs while responding promptly to facility issues, often working independently or with minimal on-site support.


Key Responsibilities

The Maintenance Technician is responsible for performing a wide range of maintenance, facilities, and technical tasks to ensure the building, grounds, and equipment are kept in safe, functional, and presentable condition. This role requires working knowledge of various trade fundamentals, including general repairs, painting, carpentry, groundskeeping, and basic electrical work. The technician also operates and maintains plant operation equipment such as boilers and chillers.


Major Duties and Responsibilities

  • Performs grounds maintenance including trimming hedges, mowing lawns, trash and weed cleanup, leaf blowing, and other landscaping tasks.
  • Conducts periodic cleaning of windows and outside entrances.
  • Completes assigned work orders in a timely and professional manner.
  • Lubricates equipment according to the Preventative Maintenance Schedule.
  • Inspects, tests, and maintains emergency equipment (generators, fire extinguishers, etc.) per the Preventative Maintenance Schedule.
  • Performs painting and minor carpentry work as required.
  • Maintains power equipment and hand tools in good working condition.
  • Executes minor preventative maintenance tasks as assigned.
  • Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to keep all equipment in proper working order, contributing to a safe environment for staff and visitors.
  • May be required to work extended hours or respond to emergencies outside of regular working hours.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Working knowledge of multiple trade fundamentals (carpentry, painting, basic electrical, grounds maintenance, etc.).
  • Ability to operate and maintain various types of plant equipment (boilers, chillers, generators, etc.).
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to read and follow preventative maintenance schedules and work orders.
  • Physical stamina and ability to perform manual labor, including lifting, bending, and working outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Reliable and safety-conscious with a strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently or as part of a team.

Working Conditions

  • This position involves both indoor and outdoor work.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb ladders, work in confined spaces, and perform tasks at various heights.
  • Exposure to varying temperatures, noise, and occasional biohazard areas.

title: Transmission Project Manager Supervisor
description:
Engineering excellence, built on people-first values.



At LUZCO, we’re more than an engineering firm — we’re a familia. We pair technical excellence with a culture rooted in respect, flexibility, and genuine care for one another. Here, you're known by name, supported as a whole person, and encouraged to bring your authentic self to work with competitive benefits, and the flexibility to support life both inside and outside of work.


We’re proud to be a 2025 and 2026 Best Place to Work in St. Louis and a woman-owned, minority-owned boutique firm, delivering impactful engineering solutions in a workplace where people feel valued and empowered to grow.




Why You’ll Love LUZCO

  • Benefits that take care of you: Top-notch medical, dental, and vision insurance; a competitive 401k match; generous PTO; student loan repayment assistance; and an employee recognition platform that celebrates your wins big and small.
  • Flexibility that fits your life: We get that life doesn’t always stick to a schedule. You’ll work with your supervisor to create a schedule that’s flexible and works for both you and the team.
  • Diversity that fuels innovation: Our team brings together a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. That diversity isn’t just something we talk about; it’s what drives our creativity and helps us find better ways to solve problems.
  • Growth that feels personal: Whether you’re continuing your education, earning new certifications, or stepping into new challenges, we’re here to help you grow in the direction that’s right for you. You’ll collaborate with experienced mentors and leaders who want to see you succeed.
  • A culture that gives back: We’re passionate about our communities. Every year, we dedicate paid time off for volunteering and encourage our team to use their talents to make a difference whether that’s mentoring students, serving local nonprofits, or getting hands-on in community projects.
  • A workplace that feels like you: We keep things relaxed and welcoming. Expect weekly happy hours, team lunches, a stocked kitchen, dogs in the office, and a casual dress code. It’s a space where you can be yourself and do your best work.



The Role



We are seeking an experienced Transmission Project Management Supervisor to lead and support the successful delivery of large-scale electric transmission and utility infrastructure projects. In this role, you will mentor a team of Transmission Project Managers while overseeing project performance, budget forecasting, and compliance across a portfolio of complex capital projects.


This position plays a key role in ensuring projects are delivered safely, on schedule, and within budget while maintaining strong alignment with client expectations and regulatory requirements.


What Your Day Will Look Like

  • Lead and mentor Transmission Project Managers through all phases of electric transmission projects, including initiation, routing and siting, engineering and design, procurement, construction, commissioning, energization, and project closeout.
  • Oversee project performance by monitoring schedule, cost, safety, risk, and quality metrics to ensure successful delivery and client satisfaction.
  • Manage capital project forecasts for a portfolio of transmission projects ranging from approximately $50M–$100M, including tracking spend and communicating budget updates or variances to stakeholders.
  • Review and support project governance documentation, including Project Execution Plans (PEPs), project authorization packages, and other materials required for client funding and approval processes.
  • Ensure compliance with client standards and project governance processes, including stage-gate reviews, construction governance requirements, and regulatory procedures.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including engineering, environmental, permitting, supply chain, construction, and operations to support successful project execution.
  • Provide regular reporting and updates to internal leadership and client stakeholders on project performance and portfolio status.
  • Travel up to 10% for client meetings, project site visits, and stakeholder coordination.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
This is a hybrid position and must be located within 100 miles of a Mayo Clinic campus for occasional on-site expectations based on business needs.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Project Manager specializing in Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management (RCM). This role, forms and leads complex, high-impact enterprise projects that span hospital billing systems, electronic health record (EHR) integrations, and process optimization while managing scope, tracking and aligning project milestones. The ideal candidate bridges the gap between hospital financial executives, clinical documentation teams, and IT professionals to safeguard cash flow and optimize financial operations.

The Senior Project Manager (PM) works independently, assuming primary responsibility for planning, directing, coordinating and delivering project activities through the entire project life cycle (from initiation through handoff to customer) that are major/complex/business critical. The Senior PM is responsible to lead project objectives and completion on time, on budget, and in conformance to Mayo Clinic project management methodologies and standards.

The Senior PM will lead large projects that have site- or enterprise-level strategic importance. Project work has high to very high risk and risk interdependencies, multiple interrelationships, and may have major costs associated. Responsible for managing established budget. Leads and provides direction in the development and tracking of project budgets. Position requires strict adherence to budget management and guidelines of both the assigned department and the institution. Independently leads problem-solving and decision-making activities, within the scope of the project and change management process, taking reasonable and prudent actions to accomplish agreed upon project objectives. Leverages many years of experience to manage extensive projects and is highly competent in the implementation of project results. Uses advanced negotiations skills that are characterized by innovative thinking.

The use and application of Agile methodologies is important to this role. Many of the items important to an Agile process are not unique to Agile. This individual may be responsible for monitoring scrum processes and scrum meetings. They may work to increase efficiency, motivate the team, and advocate for changes that will ensure quality and timeliness.

Leading project teams may include the following not already specified above:

  • Guiding teams on Agile practices and values to implement critical projects
  • Assessing maturity of the team and organization and coaching the team to higher levels of maturity, at a pace that is sustainable
  • Removing impediments and blockers or guiding the team to do so; escalating to management when appropriate
  • Building a trusting and safe environment where problems can be raised and resolved
  • Facilitating getting the work done without coercion, assigning, or dictating the work
  • Facilitating discussion, decision making, and conflict resolution
  • Supporting and educating the Product Owner, especially on creating the product backlog and ongoing backlog refinement.

May have direct and indirect reports and be in a position to employ and guide the project staff in a goal-oriented way within projects. The Senior Project Manager leads and demonstrates project-focused culture at Mayo Clinic and also advises/provides mentorship to other staff regarding project management practices, methods, and standards.

Performs additional job-related functions as detailed by immediate supervisor.

Bachelor's degree with 10 years’ experience in Project Management and business-related activities or master's degree with 7 years’ experience in Project Management. Education preference: project management, business administration, agile/scrum, management. Active (unexpired) Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is required.

Candidates should also include any certifications they have, which do not supersede the PMP certification, which may include but are not necessarily limited to Certified Product Management, Certified Scrum Master (CSM), Advanced Certified Scrum Master (A-CSM), PMI Agile Certified Practitioner, Risk Management Professional (RMP) and/or Certified Scrum Professional (CSP).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ability to facilitate and guide decision-making under high pressure.
  • Ability to track/manage key milestones of projects, initiatives, and programs.
  • Bridges complex IT systems, clinical documentation, and hospital financial performance.
  • Experience leading implementations or optimizations for major Electronic Health Records (EHR) and/or billing software i.e. Epic.

Authorization to work and remain in the United States, without necessity for Mayo Clinic sponsorships now, or in the future (for example, be a U.S. Citizen, national, or permanent resident, refugee, or asylee). Mayo Clinic does not participate in the F-1 STEM OPT extension program.

title: Food Services Associate
description:

Closing Date: September 10, 2026

This position is being recruited to support the Reactivation Care Centre (RCC). Start dates will vary and will be staggered between September and November 2026, in alignment with operational readiness, anticipated patient volumes, and the phased implementation of RCC services, and are subject to change based on operational requirements.

Start Date: Pending kitchen renovation completion and tenant occupancy.

Position Summary
This position supports safe, efficient, and patient-centered food service operations in a healthcare environment. Responsibilities include food preparation and portioning, patient tray assembly and delivery, warewashing, sanitation, food cart distribution, and maintaining clean and organized work areas. The Food Services Associate follows established food safety, infection prevention and control, and workplace health and safety procedures to ensure quality meal service and contribute to the well-being of patients and residents.

Duties

  • Prepare and portion menu items such as sandwiches, salads, desserts, entrées, soups, vegetables, and nourishments according to production requirements and standardized recipes.
  • Assemble patient meal trays accurately according to tray tickets, diet orders, textures, consistencies, and portioning requirements.
  • Assemble and deliver bulk food and supply items to patient care units.
  • Complete meal trays by adding final items such as beverages, desserts, and snacks as required.
  • Record food temperatures and complete required food safety documentation.
  • Deliver meal trays to patients while ensuring accurate patient identification and adherence to infection prevention and control practices.
  • Set up, stock, replenish, clean, and sanitize food service stations, equipment, utensils, and work areas.
  • Complete daily and scheduled cleaning assignments to maintain compliance with food safety and public health standards.
  • Distribute, retrieve, load, and unload food carts for meal service.
  • Participate in warewashing operations, including dishwashing, stripping trays, offloading, racking dishes, handling cutlery, cleaning equipment, removing waste, and maintaining a clean dish room.
  • Follow all food safety, infection prevention and control, workplace health and safety, and safe work practice requirements, including proper use of equipment and regular hand hygiene, PPE, and dress code.
  • Work collaboratively with team members and perform assigned duties in food production, patient meal service, sanitation, warewashing, and related areas.
  • Required to work at both UHN West Park Healthcare Centre and UHN Reactivation Care Centre locations based on operational requirements.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.
  • At minimum, completion of high school or recognized equivalent;
  • Food Handler Certificate, required (documentation to be provided within 60 days of hire);
  • 3-6 months practical and related experience and/or 1-3 months on the job training;
  • Previous food service experience, preferably in a healthcare, long-term care, or commercial food service environment.
  • Knowledge of therapeutic diets, texture modified diets, fluid consistencies, and meal service requirements in a healthcare setting.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.
  • Basic mathematical skills and the ability to follow recipes, production tallies, and written instructions.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and with minimal supervision, as well as within a team environment.
  • Strong organizational, time management, and attention-to-detail skills.
  • Ability to safely operate and maintain food service equipment.
  • Physical ability to perform the duties of the position, including prolonged standing, walking, lifting, pushing, pulling, bending, and repetitive tasks.
  • Ability to meet production schedules and service timelines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Availability to work a rotation of two weekends on and one weekend off and regularly rotating between morning, afternoon, and evening shifts.
  • Satisfactory work performance and attendance record.
  • Demonstrated commitment to patient-centered care and the Centre's mission, vision, and values.
  • Awareness of factors affecting the safety of patients, staff, and visitors.

Why join UHN?

In addition to working alongside some of the most talented and inspiring healthcare professionals in the world, UHN offers a wide range of benefits, programs and perks. It is the comprehensiveness of these offerings that makes it a differentiating factor, allowing you to find value where it matters most to you, now and throughout your career at UHN.

  • Government organization and a member of the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP )
  • Close access to Transit and UHN shuttle service
  • A flexible work environment
  • Opportunities for development and promotions within a large organization
  • Additional perks (multiple corporate discounts including: travel, restaurants, parking, phone plans, auto insurance discounts, on-site gyms, etc.)

Current UHN employees must have successfully completed their probationary period, have a good employee record along with satisfactory attendance in accordance with UHN's attendance management program, to be eligible for consideration.

All applications must be submitted before the posting close date.

UHN uses email to communicate with selected candidates. Please ensure you check your email regularly. At University Health Network (UHN), artificial intelligence technologies may be used to assist in the screening, assessment, and selection of candidates for this position.

Please be advised that a Criminal Record Check may be required of the successful candidate. Should it be determined that any information provided by a candidate be misleading, inaccurate or incorrect, UHN reserves the right to discontinue with the consideration of their application.

title: Senior Director Lab Services - Oregon Market
description:
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

The Senior Market Area Director, Laboratory Services will serve as the key administrative leader in coordinate key laboratory initiatives with Market Chief Executive leaders, with direct oversight of multiple laboratories. This position will be in constant collaboration with system and Division organizational leadership in developing and implementing laboratory performance improvement within the service area.

The Senior Market Area Director, Laboratory Services in concert with the Division Executive Director Clinical Lab provides strategic leadership as well as financial and operational management and direction to the laboratories within the market area.

Attributes critical to success include the ability to make difficult decisions in the context of the political, regulatory, and economic environment and consistent with the overall system strategy he/she is accountable for developing, implementing, and managing a matrix business model that supports the Market Area, Division, and System Strategic Goals for an integrated healthcare delivery system. The Service Area Director will work in a dyad relationship, with administrative oversight for Anatomic Pathology and Clinical Laboratory Services to guide the comprehensive, strategic, and tactical planning and operations of all laboratory services across the Service Area.

The position of Senior Market Area Director, Laboratory requires experience developing and implementing both short and long range business plans, coordinating service area with system strategies, analyzing and managing financial performance, maintaining positive physician relationships and coordinating all laboratory services to ensure optimal synergies of service, quality and affordability. The Senior Market Director must be able to navigate politics without becoming paralyzed by them thereby delaying critical decisions; he/she must be a change advocate who is able to sell the future vision of the Division and System of Laboratories strategy presented in the Reducing Clinical Variation (RCV) vision.

Initial focus of the Senior Market Director, Laboratory Services will be to work with the Division Executive Director for Clinical Lab to implement changes within the Market Area consistent with the parameters and goals developed as part of the of the RCV laboratory initiative. Long term responsibilities include ongoing financial and operational guidance to Chief Executive Leaders and ministry Leaders.

•Coordinating with the Division Executive Director Clinical Lab for implementation activities for transforming laboratory services within the market area.
•Collaborate with senior leadership in the Market Area and Division for long range strategic planning activities promoting excellence, maximizing system integration in clinical practice, improving the patient care experience and enhancing the value proposition of delivered services.

title: HEAD OF SENIOR SCHOOL (7-12) POR 4
description:
HEAD OF SENIOR SCHOOL (7-12) POR 4

Commencing January 2027

The POR role is a minimum 4-year engagement, whilst the teaching role is permanent. Employment is in accordance with the South Australian Catholic Schools Enterprise Agreement 2020 or its successor.

Position Information Document: HEAD OF SENIOR SCHOOL (7-12) PID 2027.pdf

St Francis de Sales College invites applications from experienced Teachers to join our vibrant school community set within the beauty of the Adelaide Hills.
The successful applicant will lead the school community in alignment with Catholic identity and Mercy values, fostering a culture of excellence in teaching, learning, and wellbeing. This role is central to achieving high-quality educational outcomes, supporting staff development, and upholding the College’s mission, vision and strategic priorities. As a key member of the leadership team, the Head of Senior School (7-12) cultivates a collaborative, high-trust environment that supports students’ academic, pastoral, spiritual, and wellbeing needs. The role works closely with the College Leadership Team, POR’s and teaching staff to ensure the delivery of engaging, effective learning programs aligned with the College’s vision for excellence.
With oversight of processes that support diverse learning needs, the Head of Senior School (7-12) monitors student outcomes, leads data-informed interventions, and ensures growth beyond benchmarks. Through evidence-informed and future-focused leadership, the role builds staff capacity, shapes effective systems and policies, and consistently demonstrates impact as both a leader and educator.

At St Francis de Sales College we aim to provide opportunities for the growth and development of all of our community members so they may 'be who they are and be that well.' We strive to inspire all to develop a love of learning and enable them to reach their full potential by living, through a Catholic lens, the College’s seven Heart Values of Faith; Perseverance; Compassion; Integrity; Respect; Wisdom; and Justice. This is the foundation and the essence upon which this role is based.

Our Vision
Be who you are and be that well

Our Mission
St Francis de Sales College is a community in which faith is nurtured in a Catholic Christian tradition. It does this by recognising each individual's skills and talents while appreciating and accepting their uniqueness.

The College is committed to promoting community and personal fulfilment through life enhancing relationships.

About the role
St Francis de Sales, as patron, symbolises the high hopes that are held for every St Francis de Sales student, so that, inspired and guided by his example, each child may:

Promote a culture of life through courage and responding to the challenges that life brings
Foster the engagement of faith and reason
Develop a love of learning and independent thinking
Be an ethical leader by valuing and respecting each individual, irrespective of position, wealth, racial and ethnic origin and religious beliefs
Become socially responsible contributor in their community and to society
Acquire virtue and wisdom and respond generously to others, throughout their life

A good education is the greatest gift we can give our children as they thrive in a safe, supportive learning environment. At St Francis de Sales College, we welcome you to ensure that we not only meet the child’s learning needs but exceed their expectations.
For all teaching positions, the successful applicant will demonstrate a capacity to engage, challenge and support learners to achieve their potential and hold a deep belief in the capacity for every child to learn.

Our staff work collaboratively with leaders, colleagues, parents/caregivers and others as applicable to facilitate positive learning for our students and engage in educational reform. St Francis de Sales College is committed to supporting and providing teachers with relevant professional learning opportunities to support their teaching practice.

KEY RESPONSIBILITES
Support the Principal in, but not limited to:

Faith Leadership and Catholic Identity

Promote and enhance the Catholic identity and Mercy ethos of the College, ensuring faith, values and traditions are embedded in all aspects of College life.

Educational Leadership and Student Growth

Lead and manage teaching, learning, and wellbeing to ensure every student experiences academic progress, personal development, and holistic achievement.

Staff Development and Professional Growth

Build staff capacity through targeted professional learning, coaching, and performance feedback to foster a culture of continuous improvement and leadership development.

Strategic and Operational Management

Oversee the implementation of strategic and operational plans, policies, and compliance requirements to ensure the effective and efficient functioning of the school.

Community Engagement and Relationships

Foster positive, respectful, and collaborative relationships with students, staff, families, and the wider community to strengthen engagement and shared purpose.

Safe and Inclusive School Culture

Ensure a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment that promotes student wellbeing, belonging, equity and a consistent R-12 approach to behaviour management for all members of the school community.

Collaborative Leadership and System Alignment

Collaborate with school leadership, staff, and external agencies to align with system priorities and drive shared educational goals.

Monitoring and Accountability

Monitor and report on student progress, wellbeing, and school performance using data-informed practices to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.
Undertake other duties as required by the Principal (or delegate).

PERSON SPECIFICATIONS

A commitment to personal growth and development as demonstrated by post graduate studies and engagement with leadership formation (i.e. Grad Cert, Masters, CESA Aspiring Leaders Program).
Appropriate academic qualifications, suitable experience and a background relevant to the position.
Currently at, or working towards, Highly Accomplished or Lead Teacher career stage (Australian Professional Standards for Teachers), which will be highly regarded.
Significant and impactful experience as an educator, preferably within a Catholic school context, with demonstrated commitment to the mission of the College.
Proven capacity to translate College strategic direction into operational priorities, actions and measurable outcomes.
Ability to lead and influence high-quality pedagogical practice, including modelling exemplary practice, coaching and developing staff to improve teaching and learning outcomes.
Proven ability to hold staff accountable for performance while fostering a culture of excellence, including setting clear expectations, monitoring practice, providing feedback, and ensuring continuous improvement in teaching and learning.
Demonstrated leadership of whole-College improvement initiatives, using data to drive outcomes and embed evidence-informed and evolving best practice.
Proven capability to lead and manage change, including influencing staff practice and embedding sustainable improvements aligned to College priorities.
Strong capability to lead teams and complex projects and programs including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Ability to build staff capability, resilience and adaptability, enabling effective response to change and evolving College priorities.
Highly developed interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence, guide and build professional relationships with a range of stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of policy, compliance and reporting requirements, and the effective use of systems (e.g. LMS) to ensure consistency and accountability.
Highly developed professional judgement, with the ability to operate with autonomy, integrity, resilience and discretion.
Commitment to continuous improvement in teaching and learning.
Capacity to navigate complex, sensitive and high-pressure situations with integrity, confidentiality, resilience, courage and initiative.
Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy while working collaboratively and maintaining alignment with College priorities and leadership direction.
All teaching staff are expected to meet the obligations of the Teacher PID.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Registration (or eligibility for registration) as a teacher in South Australia.
Act in accordance with the CESA Code of Conduct and the Charter for Staff in Catholic Schools in South Australia.
Hold a current acceptable Working with Children Check (WWCC) clearance & screening to work in Catholic Education South Australia.
Hold current certification in Responding to Risks of Harm, Abuse and Neglect in Education and Care Settings.
First Aid Qualification as directed by the College.
As a worker, comply with the SA Work Health and Safety Act 2012 and, while at work, take reasonable care for their own health and safety.

To be considered for this position, applicants are required to please submit the following:

  • Resume - Covering letter outlining the following (2 A4 pages max)

your experience relevant to the role
what has motivated you to apply and
what you hope to contribute to the school community
Resume with the names of 3 current referees (including current line manager).
Complete CESAs Dayforce screening requirements

Applications Close: 14 September 2026

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer
description:
Salary Range: $100,000.00 To $120,000.00 Annually

SJC stands as Canada’s largest privately owned communications company, distinguished by its portfolio of leading media brands, including Toronto Life, Chatelaine, and Maclean’s. At SJC, creativity, technology and journalism intersect to deliver content that resonates and performs. From integrated creative studios and advanced ad-tech to a portfolio of iconic media brands, we craft and distribute award-winning stories for audiences and advertisers alike. Partnering with organizations across North America, we build marketing solutions that inform, inspire and empower on every platform—from print to emerging digital channels. Our influence—and a 22-year streak on Canada’s Best Managed Companies list—reflects a culture committed to excellence and constant evolution. To learn more about our organization, please visit www.stjoseph.com

About the Role

Our engineering team is seeking a Senior Full-Stack Developer to play a key role in the engineering function for our Media organization. In this role you will be responsible for maintaining and enhancing our digital platforms that enable product, content and monetization to succeed for all stakeholders across SJC. As a senior member of the team, you will help to define technical priorities, contribute to architectural decisions, and collaborate closely with the product managers, designers, and editors to deliver high-impact solutions that maximize value for our users and revenue for our business. This role requires a proven track record of contributing to complex projects, architectural design, and quality code production, along with an appetite to learn—you'll be ramping up on our AdOps stack (Header Bidding, Google Ad Manager, and the data pipelines behind ad revenue) as part of the role, so we're looking for someone adaptable and eager to grow into that domain.

What You’ll Do in this Role:

Collaborate with other engineers as well as PMs and designers, contributing to a culture grounded in trust, teamwork, clear expectations, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Architect and develop new platform and product features using modern frameworks (TypeScript, React, Node.js) and AI technologies, taking ownership from prototype through production and potentially mentoring junior developers in the process.

Ramp up on and eventually contribute to the technical implementation of our ad stack, including Header Bidding and Google Ad Manager, working closely with our AdOps engineer.

Maintain build and deployment infrastructure. e.g. Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild, Terraform, and AWS Cloud formation.

Lead database development and administration using MySQL/MariaDB on AWS RDS Aurora.

Other duties as assigned.

Experienced engineer: 5+ years in software engineering with a track record of contributing to high-performing teams.

Adaptable and curious: comfortable picking up new domains (like AdOps/programmatic advertising) on the job, with no prior ad tech experience required.

Cross-functional partner: Proven collaborator with PMs, designers, and peers to take products from 0→1, managing expectations and delivering impact while fostering transparency and operational excellence.

Owning shared product services: authentication, content APIs, adtech, user engagement, personalization.

Shipping mobile web experiences (Next.js, React, Node, TypeScript—plus the leading edge framework that emerges tomorrow) accelerated with the use of AI coding agents.

Crushing performance & Core Web Vitals so ad viewability and subscription conversions soar.

Championing engineering culture: code quality, observability, threat modeling, blameless retrospectives.

Your Technical Skills Include:

Education: A bachelor’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.

Back-end & runtimes: Skilled in REST APIs (Golang, Python), containerization (Docker, AWS ECR/ECS/Fargate), microservices architecture, and serverless (AWS Lambda, Step Functions).

AdOps: Proficient with programmatic advertising, GAM, advertising analytics, and A/B testing.

AI-assisted coding: using AI tools to accelerate coding productivity while maintaining strict quality oversight over AI-produced code.

Data stores: Strong with relational databases (MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL); familiarity with NoSQL and column-store databases (e.g., ClickHouse) is a plus. Data engineering experience is a plus.

Delivery & edge: Hands-on CI/CD (GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild) and CDN/edge computing (Cloudflare).

AdOps: No prior experience required, but genuine interest in learning programmatic advertising, GAM, and ad analytics is expected.

PHP and WordPress experience are a plus.

  • Scholarship program available for employees’ children.

SJC Values

  • Amaze our customers: We put our customers’ evolving needs at the heart of the business and inspire through our ideas, quality and service.
  • Be relentlessly curious: We take the initiative to learn, try new things and brainstorm the next big idea.
  • Respect every individual as equal: We value diversity as the means to creativity and cultivate a collaborative environment where everyone belongs.
  • Innovate and adapt with urgency: Forward-thinking and flexible, we react quickly and boldly to change.
  • Contribute to our community: We apply our resources and passions to make a difference – for people and our planet

SJC is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer, where everyone feels welcome and has the opportunity to thrive. If you're contacted for an interview and require any accommodations to ensure a fair and equitable experience, please let our Human Resources team know. title: Infection Preventionist - The Lake Main Campus
description:
The Infection Preventionist 2 is responsible for implementing and monitoring infection control protocols within the hospital to ensure patient and staff safety. This role conducts surveillance of healthcare-associated infections, analyzes data, and educates staff on best practices for preventing the spread of infectious diseases. The position also collaborates with interdisciplinary teams to develop strategies for continuous improvement in infection prevention.

  1. Data Analysis & Reporting … 25%
    1. Utilizes CDC/NHSN guidelines and definitions of healthcare acquired infections

    2. Development of reports and graphs, analysis of data for trends, and presentation at appropriate committees.

  2. Education & Training Staff … 25%
    1. Provides education to patients, team members, visitors, families, physicians and community regarding infection prevention practices to improve.
    2. Participates in development of educational programs, patient safety and preventing/reducing infections risks.
    3. Presents infection prevention material at hospital orientation, unit-based meetings and annual education fairs.
    4. Assists Employee Health as needed.
    5. Performs as a consultant on infection risk assessments, prevention and control strategies, providing education and training and implementation of isolation protocols.
    6. Serves as a preceptor to newly hired Infection Preventionists.

  1. Policies and Procedures … 25%
    1. Reviews and researches policies and procedures annually to ensure current evidence-based practices are utilized.
    2. Participates with the education of staff for any changes in procedures or policies aimed at preventing infection.

    3. Implement any new protocols, policies, and procedures with collaboration from nursing leadership.

  2. Compliance & Regulatory … 20%
    1. Informs the appropriate organizations of any reportable diseases.
    2. Acts as a liaison with hospital and medical staff, patients and families.

  3. Other Duties as Assigned … 5%
    1. Evaluation of products and procedures aimed at improving patient care and/or reducing infections.
    2. Serves as active committee member on specific hospital committees.

Experience: 4 years clinical experience

Education: Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field. Medicine (Doctor), Nursing, Public Health, Biology, Epidemiology or Laboratory Medical Technology.

Certification: CIC (Certified in Infection Control)

title: Distribution Portfolio Engineer
description:
Engineering excellence, built on people-first values.



At LUZCO, we’re more than an engineering firm — we’re a familia. We pair technical excellence with a culture rooted in respect, flexibility, and genuine care for one another. Here, you're known by name, supported as a whole person, and encouraged to bring your authentic self to work with competitive benefits, and the flexibility to support life both inside and outside of work.


We’re proud to be a 2025 and 2026 Best Place to Work in St. Louis and a woman-owned, minority-owned boutique firm, delivering impactful engineering solutions in a workplace where people feel valued and empowered to grow.




Why You’ll Love LUZCO

  • Benefits that take care of you: Top-notch medical, dental, and vision insurance; a competitive 401k match; generous PTO; student loan repayment assistance; bonus opportunities that reward performance and impact; and an employee recognition platform that celebrates your wins big and small.
  • Flexibility that fits your life: We get that life doesn’t always stick to a schedule. You’ll work with your supervisor to create a schedule that’s flexible and works for both you and the team.
  • Diversity that fuels innovation: Our team brings together a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. That diversity isn’t just something we talk about; it’s what drives our creativity and helps us find better ways to solve problems.
  • Growth that feels personal: Whether you’re continuing your education, earning new certifications, or stepping into new challenges, we’re here to help you grow in the direction that’s right for you. You’ll collaborate with experienced mentors and leaders who want to see you succeed.
  • A culture that gives back: We’re passionate about our communities. Every year, we dedicate paid time off for volunteering and encourage our team to use their talents to make a difference whether that’s mentoring students, serving local nonprofits, or getting hands-on in community projects.
  • A workplace that feels like you: We keep things relaxed and welcoming. Expect weekly happy hours, team lunches, a stocked kitchen, dogs in the office, and a casual dress code. It’s a space where you can be yourself and do your best work.



The Role



As a Distribution Portfolio Engineer, you'll help utility clients make smarter, more strategic infrastructure investment decisions that support the reliability and future growth of the electric grid. Working at the intersection of engineering, planning, project management, and client strategy, you'll partner with stakeholders to develop long-term capital investment plans, evaluate project priorities, and help shape programs that deliver lasting value.


This role is a great fit for an engineer who enjoys looking at the bigger picture, solving complex challenges, and collaborating with a wide range of teams to drive meaningful results. You'll have the opportunity to work directly with clients, influence key planning decisions, and contribute to projects that make a real impact on the communities we serve.



What Your Day Will Look Like

  • Develop and maintain long-range capital investment portfolios for utility clients.
  • Partner with engineering, operations, project management, and client teams to identify current and future infrastructure needs.
  • Support the development and execution of multi-year capital investment plans.
  • Evaluate project priorities, funding requirements, schedules, risks, and overall portfolio impacts.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize project sequencing, improve efficiency, and maximize the value of capital investments.
  • Assist in developing project scopes, schedules, cost estimates, and funding strategies.
  • Review engineering, financial, and project data to support planning and investment decisions.
  • Analyze portfolio data to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support equipment planning efforts, including transformer and distribution asset planning.
  • Coordinate across multiple teams to address project dependencies, resource constraints, and execution challenges.
  • Contribute to process improvement initiatives, automation efforts, and portfolio management best practices.
  • Support the development of standards, templates, and governance processes that improve consistency and efficiency.
  • Provide training, knowledge sharing, and support as new planning tools and processes are implemented.
  • Candidates should be comfortable with occasional travel, including visits to client sites and utility facilities.

title: Senior Supply Chain Engineer
description:
Overview
The Senior Supply Chain Engineer is the on-site Product Engineer for an Oracle product at our Contract Manufacturer in Houston. The role turns product and supply-chain requirements into robust mass-production test execution and provides rapid factory support.

Why OCI
OCI operates at global scale, where reliable factory execution and disciplined product-quality controls directly support customer commitments. This role owns bringing new products into production and sustaining quality with an external manufacturing partner.

Org: Conducts technical assessments of supplier components at varying degrees of complexity and integration level. Works closely with design and procurement teams to execute tasks related to integrating supplier components into product development. Executes tasks within the New Product Introduction process to ensure components and supplier processes meet production requirements. Manages non-conforming components through defined processes such as sorting, labeling, and documentation. Participates in cross-functional projects by executing defined tasks aimed at enhancing product quality, reducing costs, and improving supply chain performance.

Team Responsibilities

  • Define mass-production test approaches for an assigned product during NPI.
  • Monitor external-manufacturer execution and adherence to Oracle production, quality, and security standards.
  • Analyze product and supply-chain information, including Linux-accessible connection, configuration, and test data.
  • Support local production, triage issues, collect evidence, and coordinate work with external-manufacturer and remote PE partners.

  • Execute supplier/component assessments, NPI tasks, audits, RCA/CAPA activities, and continuous-improvement work.

    Team Qualifications

  • Experience in product, manufacturing, supply-chain, test, quality, or supplier engineering.
  • Working knowledge of NPI, factory process controls, and mass-production operations.
  • Ability to analyze technical and manufacturing data; basic Linux command-line familiarity.
  • Experience collaborating with suppliers, contract manufacturers, and internal engineering or procurement partners.
  • Clear communication, independent prioritization, and sound escalation judgment in time-sensitive production environments.

Org Responsibilities


Select and Qualify Components:
-Conducts technical assessments of supplier components at varying degrees of complexity and integration level including evaluating material composition, electrical characteristics, mechanical properties, and durability.
-Conducts standard or moderately complex analysis of component reliability by gathering data, conducting tests, and ensuring adherence to industry standards.
-Works with Supplier Quality, Supply Chain Security, and Test Engineering teams to execute defined component qualification efforts.
-Reviews supplier manufacturing processes to understand quality assurance practices and contribute to quality assessments.
Supplier Engagement:
-Manages specific aspects of supplier relationships by providing technical input and ensuring adherence to performance and quality requirements.
-Executes assigned elements of audits of new and existing suppliers, focusing on production capabilities, process controls, and quality and security standards compliance.
-Develops technical insights on supplier processes and contributes to improvement initiatives.
-Works closely with design and procurement teams to execute tasks related to integrating supplier components into product development.
New Product Introduction:
-Executes tasks within the New Product Introduction (NPI) process to ensure components and supplier processes meet production requirements.
-Participates in design reviews to provide insights on component selection, manufacturability, and supplier capabilities.
-Coordinates with suppliers on specific production tasks to align with project timelines and demand forecasts.
-Assists with tasks during pilot production runs by preparing materials, collecting data, and ensuring compliance with standards.
Failure Analysis:
-Contributes to quality excursions by conducting moderately complex root cause analyses (RCA) and by recommending corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) within the supply chain.
-Performs root cause analysis tasks by executing data collection processes and collaborating with suppliers and quality teams.
-Monitors quality metrics and identifies trends that could impact component quality.
-Manages non-conforming components through defined processes such as sorting, labeling, and documentation.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
-Works with Design, Operations, Quality, and Procurement teams to execute component strategy alignment with product goals.
-Acts as a liaison between suppliers and internal teams for specific issues, facilitating communication and resolution.
-Participates in cross-functional projects by executing defined tasks aimed at enhancing product quality, reducing costs, and improving supply chain performance.
-Executes tasks during design changes, process optimizations, and supply chain transitions by -contributing data and technical insights.
-Analyzes and course corrects standard problems before communicating hurdles to management.

Core Responsibilities
Planning & Execution:
-Independently manages work, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure projects or initiatives stay on track and meet requirements. Proactively prioritizes work and adapts to resource or timeline shifts, suggesting adjustments to maintain project efficiency.
Collaboration & Partnership:
-Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others.
Problem Solving:
-Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices.
Continuous Learning:
-Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools, and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members.
Continuous Improvement:
-Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work.

title: Project Construction Technician 1
description:
Systems Planning Corporation (SPC), a subsidiary company of GAI Consultants, Inc. is seeking qualified, motivated, and skilled Lead Construction Inspector / Coordinators (Project Construction Technician 1) to provide quality assurance oversight and work performance on landfill construction projects throughout the Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern states. This is a contract position

Experience with construction quality control (CQC) or construction quality assurance (CQA) for the installation of geosynthetic liner systems at landfills is required. Individual will be responsible for observing construction activities, completing field testing of soils/earthwork, inspecting geosynthetic liner installation and completing daily reports to monitor and document Construction Activities. Individual will act as the lead CQC/CQA representative on project sites and will be responsible for interacting with the project Owner, project Contractor, third party testing laboratories, and GAI engineers to verify construction is being completed in accordance with the project plans and specifications. Individual will be responsible for managing and training other GAI construction technicians utilized for the project.

Essential Duties Include:

  • Perform routine inspections, checks, tests, and sampling procedures for power generation construction inspection.
  • Applicants must be willing to travel to the regions serviced, with infrequent project support at sites further away. Lodging (hotel) will be provided. This position is primarily field-oriented and location will vary by project support requirements.
  • Inspection areas include geosynthetic liner systems for environmental containment (landfills and above ground storage tanks), concrete testing and soils testing.
  • Follow quality control requirements and well-defined criteria using inspection tools and devices. Perform audits to ensure standards of quality are maintained.
  • Accurately document the results of the inspections, testing, and quality control checks.
  • Coordinate calibration of test equipment, tools, and devices.
  • Assist in the writing and updating of inspection procedures, protocols, and checklists.
  • Interpret prints, drawings, and schematics.
  • Assist in writing certification reports to document construction activities at the conclusion of the project
  • Interpret project specifications and be familiar with schedule and frequency of required samples and tests.
  • OSHA 10-hour Training is desired, but not required. Certification may be scheduled at time of hiring.
  • Minimum of 5 years experience in landfill construction CQC/CQA projects including geomembrane installation, structural fill placement, protective cover placement above geomembranes, installation of drainage structures, and installation of sediment ponds.
  • Certified in geosynthetic placement from a program such as the Geosynthetic Institute (GSI) – Inspector Certification Program or equivalent, certification is desired but not required. Certification may be scheduled at time of hiring.
  • American Concrete Institute (ACI) Concrete Testing Technician – Grade 1 certification is desired but not required. Certification may be scheduled at time of hiring.

General Characteristics

  • Begins assisting Task Managers and Project Manager as needed on technical aspects of the project; well-rounded in aspects of consulting and the industry.

Minimum Years of Experience

  • 10+ Years of Experience

Education

  • H.S. Graduate

Certification/Licensure

  • Driver’s License

Technical Responsibilities

  • Responsibilities involve performing and overseeing field monitoring on various multisite/phase construction projects of moderate to large scale, scope, and/or complexity, including placement of concrete, earthwork, roadway paving, buildings, structures, foundations, and building materials. Generates and substantiates reports and documentation regarding construction, materials, integration, equipment, and operations

  • Travel details:
    • In state and out of state as required

title: Cloud Engineer
description:
We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Cloud Engineer to join our multi-million dollar National Intelligence program supporting the Cloud Investment Multi-Cloud Management (CIMM) team. As a contributor to the Intelligence Community’s first multi-cloud initiative, you will be at the epicenter of emergent cloud computing technologies, establishing a foundation that will evolve to include all agencies within the IC. As a Senior Cloud Engineer, you will advise Government IT teams on the design and build of single- or multi-cloud computing architecture solutions that meet mission requirements, and develop future technology and architectural advancements to support the Government’s architectural strategy, cloud migration, and continued evolution.

Your responsibilities will include the following:

  • Advising senior business and technical personnel to aid in the delivery of robust, scalable cloud architectures that meet or exceed mission requirements
  • Serving as a cloud agnostic advocate and helping to educate the Government customer on cloud services appropriate to meet mission requirements
  • Providing advisory services to maintain and evolve the future-state service provider-authorized, multi-cloud architecture, and knowledge database based on ever-changing IC mission needs and ensuring optimization of cost, consumption, and performance of services are achieved across all Cloud Service Providers (CSPs)
  • Developing a baseline multi-cloud architecture methodology and framework for implementation within the C2E multi-cloud ecosystem
  • Supporting the development and maintenance of data models, data dictionaries, data maps, and other architecture artifacts across the enterprise
  • Designing all cloud solutions in alignment with applicable policies, standards, and practices
  • Providing creative and innovative architectural solutions to ill-defined requirements
  • Reviewing and accessing impact of proposed scope changes to future architectures
  • May be required to provide cloud agnostic technical guidance in the formulation of customer multi-cloud work statements

Required:

  • Must be a US Citizen
  • Must have an active TS/SCI with Polygraph
  • Bachelors and nine (9) years or more experience; Masters and seven (7) years or more experience ; PhD or JD and four (4) years or more experience.
  • Five (5) or more years of experience in a cloud and/or hybrid environment (additional 4 years of experience in lieu of degree)
  • Five (5) or more years of demonstrated experience in one or more of the following activities:
    • IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS services (e.g., compute, storage, network, security, administration, automation, application services, and databases)
    • Designing and deploying cloud solutions to Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), IBM Cloud, or Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
    • Large-scale data architecture, data modeling, database design, and information systems implementation
  • Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in enterprise data strategy, data governance practices, data stewardship principles, data standards, and metadata management best practices
  • Ability to translate requirements into end-to-end designs for systems that involve multiple interfaces and support data repositories
  • Strong customer service skills, teaming skills, and the ability to collaborate within a cross-functional team, as well as the CSPs (AWS, Azure, Google, IBM, and Oracle)
  • Certification(s):
    • AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
    • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
    • Cloud related (e.g., DevOps, Security, and/or ML)

Desired:

  • Certifications in any of the following CSPs:
    • Azure
    • OCI
    • GCP
    • IBM
  • Experience as a cloud agnostic architect
  • Strong analysis and quality assessment skills
  • Experience with successful full life cycle cloud development projects
  • Experience with various Linux and Microsoft Windows OSs distributions
  • Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) and databases
  • Experience migrating both custom built and enterprise apps to and from on-prem to cloud
  • Experience debugging performance and technical issues
  • Experience building and deploying systems in the cloud using continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) frameworks and infrastructure automation
  • Excellent written and verbal communications skills
  • Ability to work well independently and within a team environment
  • Ability to explain technical issues clearly and accurately to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Demonstrated ability to adjust to change priorities

title: Senior SIU (Claims Fraud) Investigator
description:
We are searching for a Senior SIU Investigator -- someone who works well in a fast-paced setting. In this position, you will assist the Director of Controls and Compliance and the Special Investigative Unit Manager in conducting investigations into suspected incidents of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse (FWA). This includes data mining for potential intakes, performing preliminary analysis on provider cases, and working on projects focused on preventing, detecting, and correcting fraud, waste, and abuse.

Job Duties & Responsibilities
• Conducts Fraud, Waste and Abuse (FWA) and related compliance investigations.
• Completes detailed and extensive investigations in adherence with organization’s procedures and best practices. Gather evidence and determine potential recoveries.
• Independently develops and executes appropriate investigation strategy for assigned cases. Leads in-depth interviews of participants, witnesses or affected parties.
• Researches and prepares cases for clinical and legal reviews.
• Conducts reviews of flagged claims and suspected FWA, identifying opportunities for improving payment accuracy and preventing FWA.
• Analyzes compliance and FWA cases for root cause, trends, and tracks data to translate findings and develop processes for improvement or investigation.
• Prepares accurate, timely, unbiased, and detailed written reports and case summaries in compliance with corporate standard operating procedures and guidelines documenting investigative results.
• Prepares referrals for preliminary investigations, including Requesting medical records, creating forms, reports and updating logs.
• Facilitates the recovery of inappropriate payments from FWA matters.
• Drafts recoupment letters for FWA findings.
• Supports other investigators in SIU operations.
• Trains SIU Investigator on Investigation procedures.
• Maintains case management log with investigative notes, reports, and summaries.
• Proactively collaborates with line of business personnel to generate referrals.
• Partners with the federal and state agencies on data requests, projects, investigations, and meetings.
• Communicates investigation outcomes to line of business personnel and partners to implement provider and other compliance/ SIU related edits when appropriate.
• Maintains organization’s confidential information in accordance with corporate policies, as well as state and federal laws, rules, and regulations regarding confidentiality.

Skills & Requirements
• High School Diploma or GED with preferred bachelor's degree
• 6 years’ experience in claims examination, adjusting, fraud detection, or investigations preferably in a healthcare environment
• Preferred certification as an Accredited Health Care Fraud Investigator (AHFI) by the National Healthcare Anti-Fraud Association (NHCAA)

Children’s Advantage

Full-Time, 40 Hours/Week

title: Senior Loss Prevention Analyst
description:
As a Senior Loss Prevention Analyst, you'll be a trusted analytical partner responsible for turning complex operational and financial data into meaningful business insights. You'll evaluate trends, identify areas of risk, investigate process gaps, and develop reporting solutions that support strategic decision-making across the organization.

Success in this role requires a blend of technical expertise, analytical curiosity, and strong business acumen. title: Head of Programme Coordination and Innovation Unit (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive, and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration.

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories:

Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and direct supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission (DCoM), in coordination with the Programme Managers, Senior Resource Management Officer, Heads of Sub-Offices IOM West and Central of Africa Regional Office (RO) and IOM’s Headquarters (HQ), the Head of Programme Coordination and Innovation Unit (PCIU) will be responsible for the management and coordination of unit activities, including programme and project conceptualization, proposal development, Monitoring and Evaluation, support the Country Office (CO) strategic planning and relationships with UN, donors and the Government of Nigeria, particularly in relation to the operational aspects of programmes/projects and resource mobilization.

  1. Manage and supervise the staff of the Mission Support and Innovation Unit, ensuring their effective and timely performance of development, implementation, and reporting tasks for IOM Nigeria’s programmes/projects according to institutional guidance.
  2. Assess potential project and funding opportunities, prepare project proposals and concept notes in the areas of interest to IOM Nigeria, and review and improve project reports, fact sheets and other documents in coordination with relevant Programme/Project managers and programme units.
  3. Support the coordination and evaluation of programme and project activities of IOM Nigeria to ensure timely and effective implementation and quality reporting and advise the DCoM of the corrective measures that may be needed.
  4. Support liaison with donors, project partners, other IOM Country Offices, RO, and HQ to facilitate coordinated project implementation and synergies and to make recommendations on donor/partner engagement.
  5. Provide advice for the mainstreaming of relevant African Union, Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), West African Community, Intergovernmental Authority on Development and Common Market for West Africa policies and frameworks into internal frameworks, policies, as well as national-level programming and design.
  6. Keep abreast of and analyse migration issues, policies, and emerging trends, identify priorities, and recommend actions to the Deputy Chief of Mission in relation to risks and opportunities for IOM.
  7. Identify priorities, challenges and issues to be addressed within the country office as appropriate and propose corrective actions.
  8. Provide support and guidance to Programme/Project Managers and other project staff on programme/project implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and quality assurance.
  9. Participate in relevant UN and inter-agency meetings and mechanisms to facilitate the integration of IOM programmes into inter-agency processes and the mainstreaming of migration into Common Country Analysis and Cooperation frameworks.
  10. Support IOM Nigeria in working with respective national counterparts to facilitate cooperation, external relations, and liaison activities.
  11. In close coordination with the Information Management System Officer, provide evidence-based information on IOM Nigeria’s project development and fundraising efforts through targeted assessment surveys, analyses, studies, and systematic publication.
  12. Develop and disseminate communications and visibility materials, such as quarterly reports, newsletters, flash reports, etc., and respond to information requests from HQ and Regional Office.
  13. Facilitate the generation and use of knowledge to promote improved policy engagement, project development and management in Nigeria and the West and Central Africa region.
  14. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,

  • University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in the field of international migration, management, and evaluation;

  • Work experience in the field of migration issues, including operational and field experience, IOM Project Development, Management, Implementation and Monitoring systems;

  • Experience in dealing with donors on project implementation and reporting;

  • Experience and excellent understanding of the migration themes in West Africa and extensive knowledge of the arid and semi-arid regions; and,

  • Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, other national/international institutions, and Non-Governmental Organizations.

Skills

  • Knowledge in project monitoring and evaluation is required;

  • Demonstrated expertise in thematic areas relevant to project liaison, reporting, and monitoring; and,

  • Knowledge and experience of regional issues is an advantage.

Languages

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action-oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security, as well as accreditation, and any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time in Geneva, Switzerland, on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system-wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates, link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies.
